sources.title: Metformin hydrochloride extended-release tablets prescribing information
sources.publisher: DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine
sources.version_note: Current source snapshot verified during benchmark construction on 2026-09-05.

claims.paraphrased_claim: Metformin extended-release is contraindicated when eGFR is below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2.
claims.locator: Section 2.4.2, Recommended Dosage in Patients with Renal Impairment

claims.paraphrased_claim: Starting metformin extended-release is not recommended when eGFR is between 30 and 45 mL/min/1.73 m2.
claims.locator: Section 2.4.3, Recommended Dosage in Patients with Renal Impairment

claims.paraphrased_claim: For a patient already taking metformin whose eGFR later falls below 45, continuing therapy requires a benefit-risk reassessment; falling below 30 triggers the label's discontinuation rule.
claims.locator: Section 2.4.4 and continuation of renal-impairment dosing instructions
